blockers.quote: "Day two hundred and sixty-seven. More dollars than atoms in the universe." (about 10^80, c09)
blockers.why: Overstates scope beyond what c09 and its source support. The source URL (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observable_universe) and verbatim quote ("approximately 10^80 hydrogen atoms, also known as the Eddington number") measure the observable universe, not the entire universe, which may be infinite. The claim row in claims.md c09 explicitly specifies "atoms in the observable universe".
blockers.fix: "Day two hundred and sixty-seven. More dollars than atoms in the observable universe." (about 10^80, c09)

blockers.quote: Counting it out loud now takes seventeen thousand years (c08).
blockers.why: Overstates precision. 2^39 seconds is approximately 17,421 years (or 17,400 years as given in the c08 quote). The claim in claims.md c08 explicitly requires the caveat "about seventeen thousand", but the draft speaks it as an exact number without "about".
blockers.fix: Counting it out loud now takes about seventeen thousand years (c08).

blockers.quote: "This morning you were given more than you had ever had in your life, added together."
blockers.why: Arithmetic error on doubling series. On day forty (2^39 = $550 billion), the new money given at midnight is 2^38 ($275 billion), which is not more than all previous days' balances added together ($550 billion), nor more than all previous credits added together ($275 billion). As correctly stated in line 37 ("Today is always your whole life so far, plus one"), it is your total balance that exceeds everything before it added together, not the morning increment.
blockers.fix: "This morning your balance is more than your whole life so far, added together."

suggestions.quote: and the day the dollars would outnumber the atoms in the universe (c09).
suggestions.fix: and the day the dollars would outnumber the atoms in the observable universe (c09).

suggestions.quote: The counting-time ladder (thirty-four years, seventeen thousand years, four and a half million years) is exact arithmetic on the research numbers
suggestions.fix: The counting-time ladder (thirty-four years, about seventeen thousand years, about four and a half million years) is rounded from exact arithmetic on the research numbers

suggestions.quote: and by day fifty-eight it overflows the number box most computers count in.
suggestions.fix: and by day fifty-eight it overflows the number box most computers count in (c06).

keep.quote: "Most money, sir, is made when a bank lends. And when a loan is repaid, the money doesn't go anywhere. It stops existing. The Bank of England wrote that down in 2014." (c03, c04)
"On most computer systems, the number box is sixty-four bits. And because the bank counts in cents, day fifty-eight overflows into a negative nineteen-digit number (c06)."
Wagenaar and Sagaria (1975) (c05): asked to extend a doubling series, people guess a small fraction of the truth, and being told doesn't fix it.
